source_anchor: CLRS §32 string matching (palindrome as classic two-pointer exercise); standard interview canon (LeetCode #125)
prompt_text: Determine whether the string "racecar" is a palindrome and print the boolean. Expected output: "true".

exec_cell.code: const s="racecar"; let p=true; for(let i=0;i<Math.floor(s.length/2);i++){if(s[i]!==s[s.length-1-i]){p=false; break;}} console.log(p);

candidate_responses.text: CORRECT: reverse-and-compare idiom — equivalent to the two-pointer scan.
WRONG: index arithmetic is s[s.length-i] instead of s[s.length-1-i] — the first iteration reads s[7] (undefined) and concludes not-palindrome.
candidate_responses.code: const s="racecar"; let p=true; for(let i=0;i<s.length;i++){if(s[i]!==s[s.length-i]){p=false; break;}} console.log(p);

candidate_responses.text: CARGO-CULT: split / every / palindrome vocabulary, but the predicate compares adjacent characters (s[i] vs s[i+1]) rather than mirrored ends.
